## Findings ledger
- [D5.DOC2.F4] The conclusion concedes that the open society may solve social problems, but preserves a critique of its systemic consequences and rejects a renewed totalizing solution — dim: concession_consequence — concession: “The ‘open society’” may be capable of solving social problems — response: the text stresses that its realization generates new social and ecological problems and calls instead for sober containment of unplanned effects — consequence: problem-solving capacity is retained as a limited possibility, while any promise of final freedom, happiness, or reconciliation is rejected — anchor: "The \"open society\"—to return to the formula coined by Karl Popper—may well be capable of solving social problems." — doc: religion2022 — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

sections_inspected: Religious and Secular Critique of Money
The Unbounding of Markets as the Basis of Modern Capitalism
The Intransparency of World Society to Itself: Luhmann and Hayek
The Religious Worldview and the Consequences of Its Dethronement
Universalism and the Contingency of the World: A Comparative Perspective on Capitalism and Religion
scope_outcomes.criterion: A finding must identify an acknowledged limit, qualification, or concession and explain whether the text answers, distinguishes, preserves, or leaves open the affected conclusion.
scope_outcomes.basis: The text repeatedly acknowledges capitalism’s historical efficacy and worldly performance while narrowing claims about fulfilled expectations, ultimate religious meaning, reconciliation, and final problem-solving.
limitations: The assessment concerns the supplied text and its cited positions; no additional works were inspected.
